newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-What's Happening in Australian Sport.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-What's Happening in Australian Sport.

text.p: It's play-offs time for AFL and rugby league, with the top eight teams from both codes battling out the first round of their complicated finals series this weekend.

The Sydney Swans have captured the imagination of the often fickle Sydney public, with tickets for the AFL minor premiers' match against eighth-placed Hawthorn on Saturday night at the Sydney Cricket Ground sold out in a couple of hours on Thursday.

The match will be shown live on television to satisfy those who missed out on tickets. The big question in the lead-up to the match is whether star forward Tony Lockett will play for the Swans, with the AFL's leading goal-kicker missing training for the second week in a row through injury.
The AFL finals series kicks off on Friday night when third-placed Brisbane take on sixth-placed Essendon in Brisbane.
West Coast and defending premiers Carlton, fourth and fifth respectively, play in Perth on Saturday afternoon.
North Melbourne then play Geelong at the Melbourne Cricket Ground on Sunday.
In an increasingly arcane finals format, the two lowest ranked teams from the top eight who lose this weekend will be eliminated from the finals series.
The top two ranked winners advance to the preliminary finals in two weeks, with the remaining four battling it out next week. RUGBY LEAGUE

The play-off format for the Australian Rugby League (ARL) is almost as complicated and begins on Friday night when fifth-placed Cronulla take on eighth-placed Western Suburbs in an elimination final at Parramatta Stadium.
The second elimination semifinal sees Canberra and St George, sixth and seventh respectively on the ARL ladder, meet at the Sydney Football Stadium (SFS).
The first qualification final sees second-placed Brisbane take on North Sydney, who finished third, at Suncorp Stadium on Saturday night.
On Sunday ARL minor premiers Manly play fourth-placed Sydney City at the SFS.
The losers of the two elimination finals bow out, with the winners going on to play the losers of the two qualifying finals next week.
The winners of the two qualifying finals get a week off and then play the winners from the second week of finals matches.
CRICKET
Australia's match against India in the Singer World Series limited overs tournament in Colombo was postponed to Friday after being rained out on Thursday.

The two teams are playing for the right to meet hosts Sri Lanka in the tournament final, with Sri Lanka living up to their World Cup-winning form by cruising through their matches against Australia, India and Zimbabwe in startlingly easy fashion.
Australia will benefit if the match against India is again rained out, with Ian Healy's Australians assured of a place in the final by virtue of a superior run rate.
TENNIS
Australia is guaranteed a place in the U.S. Open men's doubles final at the weekend, with Mark Philippoussis and Pat Rafter due to play top seeds Todd Woodbridge and Mark Woodforde in the semifinals.

Philippoussis and Rafter beat Dutch pair Henrik Jan Davids and Sjeng Schalken 6-3 6-4 in the quarter-finals while Atlanta Olympic gold medallists and three-time Wimbledon winners "the Woodies" had a similarly easy match against Canada's Sebastien Lareau and Alex O'Brien of the United States.
